verdict.rationale: Swell documents a backend API that covers core commerce resources (products, stock adjustments, purchase links) and a runtime schema endpoint listing every model. Custom models extend both the dashboard and the backend API, and admin workflows can be built as custom frontends. That points toward API-first design, but no evidence states that the UI and API have full parity, and no machine-readable OpenAPI spec was found. missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement of UI-to-API parity, API coverage evidence for UI features such as theme editing, drag-and-drop category management, reports and team roles/permissions, a published OpenAPI spec, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Build frontends for storefronts and admin workflows with any framework.
Add functionality to the dashboard and backend API with custom models.
One call returns a store’s whole schema at runtime: every model—standard, merchant custom and app-installed alike—with field types and relationships.
Official libraries for the Swell API are available for Node and PHP.
Stock adjustments are used to keep track of inventory changes over time.
